judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic claims all check out: P'(2, -2), Q'(-6, -2), R'(-7, 2), A'B' = 5 from (-1,-4) to (3,-1), C'D' = 5 from (4,1) to (7,5), E'F' = 4, and the corrected G' = (6, 3). But the claim that this packet is clean on verification is refuted by two artifacts. (1) Problem 6 prints FIVE fill-in slots - E' = (__,__), F' = (__,__), E'F' = __ - and verify.json id 6 holds only four entries (-a at a=-3, -b at b=5, -b at b=1, and the distance); the F' x-coordinate is never checked, and the delivered Quick Answers row reads "6. 3, -5, -1, 4", four values against five blanks. (2) Problem 7 prints an explicit \underline{\hspace{4.5cm}} writing rule for "Which transformation did Sam actually perform?" - a named-error diagnosis - and verify.json id 7 carries only two `eval` entries with no `manual`, so gate_log.txt reports exactly one manual item (problem 8) and final_response.md repeats that claim. The judge reviewed one manual item and did not notice a second open response was never routed for review.

strengths_to_preserve: The answer key's problem 3 hands the student two independent self-checks that do not need the key: both spokes measure sqrt(53), and the slopes 7/2 and -2/7 multiply to -1 - and it then names the clockwise image (7, -2) as the direction-error signature.

Problem 8's manual entry is a real marking guide: full credit needs the motion named (rotation, 90 deg, counterclockwise, about the origin), the rule checked on each vertex, and a distance-preservation argument; "they look the same size and shape" is explicitly listed as insufficient, and a 270 deg clockwise description is pre-accepted.

Every problem sets a pre-plotted grid beside the coordinate rule, so an algebra slip and a plotting slip produce visibly different failures - the sheet's own directions tell the student to trust the algebra and re-count the grid.

Problem 7's two declared traps are per-coordinate (x kept at -6, y negated to -3), so the key's Common wrong answers block distinguishes the x-axis reflection from a sign slip rather than lumping them.

root_causes.description: The verify JSON was written per computed VALUE rather than per printed slot, so a coordinate that repeats an earlier expression (F' x = -(-3) = 3, the same value as E' x) was dropped instead of being declared as its own response.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 6 prints \ansblank five times (E' pair, F' pair, E'F'); verify.json id 6 contains four entries, none of which is the F' x-coordinate.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers row 6 is "3, -5, -1, 4" - a grader reading only the bank cannot tell which of the five blanks the four numbers belong to.
The key's prose does give F' = (3, -1), but the 3 is unboxed because no verify entry backs it.

root_causes.description: An open diagnosis printed with its own writing rule was left out of the manual set because the problem also contained machine-checkable coordinates; the presence of `eval` entries made the problem look covered.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 7 prints "Which transformation did Sam actually perform?" followed by \underline{\hspace{4.5cm}}; verify.json id 7 has two `eval` entries and no `manual` entry.
gate_log.txt line 44 lists a single [MANUAL] item (problem 8) and the summary reads "1 problem(s) need manual review (22 machine-verified)".

Problem 6 similarly asks "Which quadrant did the segment start in, and which did it land in?" with 2.2cm of workspace and no manual entry; the key answers it (second quadrant to fourth) but nothing routes it to a human.

improvements.title: Verify (or flag manual for) every response slot the worksheet prints
improvements.proposed_change: Make the verify JSON an inventory of PRINTED RESPONSES, not of terminal answers. SKILL.md should require one verify entry per answer location a problem prints (\ansblank, \ansline, \answerline, an \underline writing rule, or a table cell the student fills), with `manual` used where the response is not a value. Enforce it with a new gate wired into scripts/build.sh that segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.segment_spans, counts the answer-location macros and fill-in rules per problem, and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries for the same problem id. Here the gate must fail problem 6: five printed slots against four verify entries.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem prints five \ansblank slots against a verify id carrying four entries must make the new gate exit non-zero; adding the missing entry (or a `manual` entry) must make it exit 0. Today no gate compares slot count with entry count, so the fixture passes the whole chain - the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic gap in this run: a sheet can no longer claim complete verification while printing blanks nothing checked, and the answer key's Quick Answers bank stops shipping short rows.
improvements.risk: Sheets that use several blanks to scaffold ONE value ("x-coordinate: __ y-coordinate: __ so P' = (__, __)") will need either a coarser blank layout or a documented per-value grouping, so the gate needs a same-value exemption to avoid false failures.

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problem 7's "Which transformation did Sam actually perform?" rule and problem 6's quadrant question must each force a `manual` entry.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

case_summary: An accurate and unusually well-taught rigid-motions packet - every image coordinate, every distance check and the corrected G' = (6, 3) recompute correctly, and problem 8's marking guide is a model for open items. Two verification gaps survive the whole gate chain: problem 6 prints a fifth blank (F' x) that nothing checks, and problem 7's named-error diagnosis is printed with its own writing rule but never flagged manual, so both the gate log and final_response.md understate the human-review load by one item.
